label: late-episode-scaled reward/rare-transition and belief-toward-S1 boosts
terms: (phase == GO) * belief_lo * np.exp(ep_trial/20.) ;; (phase == D2) * (common == 0) * table(state, {1: 1, 2: -1}) * np.exp(ep_trial/20.) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) * np.exp(ep_trial/20.) ;; (phase == GO) * table(prev_action, {1: 1, 2: -1}) * np.exp(ep_trial/20.) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 1) * np.exp(ep_trial/20.) ;; (phase == D2) * (prev_reward == 1) * np.exp(ep_trial/20.) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) * (prev_common == 0) * np.exp(ep_trial/20.) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a1 S1 r") * np.exp(ep_trial/20.)
explanation: Raw GRU candidate n of unit 18. Mostly saturated near -0.95 and rising steeply late in the episode; timing alone gives R^2 0.90, so only the small residual is left to explain. Every effect beyond timing grows with episode time, so each term is scaled by exp(ep_trial/20); that scaling improves on unscaled terms (0.16 to about 0.29 dev). Observed drivers: at D1 it goes up after a rewarded previous trial, more so if that transition was rare. At GO it goes up with the ideal-observer belief that S1 is good (belief_lo), after a previous a1 choice (most after a1 S1 rewarded) and after reward. At D2 a rare transition pushes it up if the agent landed in S1 (a2 to S1) and down if it landed in S2 (a1 to S2). Test R^2 beyond timing is 0.31 (dev 0.31), at or above the profile ceilings (all 0.29, all observed 0.26), so dropping the model value/policy loses essentially nothing; the policy-decile table alone gave 0.13 and belief covers most of that at GO. The rest of the residual is persistent offsets at the window level in late-episode windows (whole windows sit 0.1-0.3 above or below the prediction), which none of the trial-history, belief, belief_cover or reward-count terms tried here captured. No future variables used.
